newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angolan president reveals strains with UNITA.
newsitem.headline: Angolan president reveals strains with UNITA.

text.p: Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos on Thursday revealed serious strains in relations with UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi, saying he had not talked with him since early August.
The comments by Dos Santos on national radio came a day after southern African leaders slammed UNITA, the former rebel movement, for delaying efforts to shore up Angola's shaky peace.
Dos Santos said he last spoke to Savimbi several days before the start of an extra-ordinary UNITA congress in mid-August to decide the future of the movement.

"After the congress of UNITA there has practically been no evolution in the implementation of the Lusaka Protocol. My last telephone conversation with Dr Savimbi occurred several days before the congress and since that dialogue has been difficult."

The president said he hoped the U.N. Security Council, reviewing its peace-keeping mandate in Angola, would pressure UNITA to fulfill its obligations under the peace plan signed in the Zambian capital Lusaka in 1994.

Eleven heads of state from the Southern African Development Community (SADC) met in the Angolan capital Luanda on Wednesday to try to end the deadlock. Savimbi did not arrive, citing "unfortunate political conditions".
The SADC group condemned Savimbi's boycott but added they would continue their contacts to get discussions going between the two Angolan leaders.
Dos Santos told the summit Angola had reached a dangerous crossroads: "We have the impression that someone wants to push the return of war...It is, however, not our wish."
Savimbi has yet to tell dos Santos personally of a decision by UNITA's congress not to accept the vice-presidency position offered him in a future unity government.
Political analysts said the UNITA leader had further isolated himself by ignoring efforts by African and Western governments to break the stalemate.
